info.title: Prospector API
info.description: External REST API for LeadIQ prospector lists and prospects.

apiKeyAuth.name: X-API-Key
apiKeyAuth.description: Send your LeadIQ API key as the `X-API-Key` header value — no prefix, no encoding.

bearerAuth.description: OAuth2 access token (JWT) issued for an audience accepted by this service.

ListRole.description: Caller's relationship to the list. `owner` means the caller created it; `collaborator` means another member granted them edit access.

phone.description: Single mobile phone. Use phones, which takes precedence

companyId.description: DataIQ company id (a search result's `companyId`). Send it whenever the person came from a search: it links the prospect to the company record, so the company is captured once instead of twice.

personId.description: DataIQ ID. Provide it for better matching and deduplication

companyId.description: DataIQ company id (the flattened `"<sourceType>-<objectId>"` form, e.g. from a company search result). Absent on entries added manually by name/domain/linkedinUrl only.
DataIQ company id in the flattened "<sourceType>-<objectId>" form, as returned by company search results. The strongest match key — send it whenever the company came from a search.

status.description: `created` — a new Salesforce record exists. `updated` — an existing record was enriched instead; only possible when the request carried `updateExisting: true` or `recordId`. `duplicates_found` — **nothing was written**; see `duplicates`. `account_choice_required` — **nothing was written**; several Accounts matched, see `accounts`, then call again with `accountId`. `record_choice_required` — **nothing was written**; several existing records could be this person, see `records`, then call again with `recordId`.

entityId.description: Salesforce id of the created/updated record. Absent on `duplicates_found`, and possible to be absent on `updated`.

savedAs.description: Which Salesforce object the export targeted, decided by the member's `Save to` setting and the org's governance — not by this API.

requestId.description: Correlation id for the export, for support lookups.

records.description: Present on `record_choice_required`: the existing Salesforce records that could be this person. Pick one and resend its `id` as `recordId`.

accounts.description: Present on `account_choice_required`: the Accounts this prospect could be filed under. Pick one and resend its `id` as `accountId`.

entityType.description: Salesforce object of the candidate, e.g. `Lead`.

id.description: Salesforce record id — send this back as `recordId`.

updatable.description: False when one-click update is switched off for this record type. It is listed so you can see the record exists, but choosing it will not work.

id.description: Salesforce Account id — send this back as `accountId`.

link.description: Opens the Account record in the connected Salesforce org.

parentName.description: Parent Account name, when this one sits under another — often what tells two near-identical Accounts apart.

force.description: Create the record even though Salesforce reported possible duplicates. Only send `true` after a previous call returned `status: "duplicates_found"` and a human confirmed none of the candidates is the same person. Forcing blindly is the main way duplicate Leads get into a customer CRM.

accountId.description: The Salesforce Account to file this prospect under as a Contact. Only meaningful for orgs whose "Save to" is "Create Contact if Account Exists, Otherwise Lead". Send it after a previous call returned `status: "account_choice_required"` and a human picked one of the `accounts`. Sending it skips the Account search entirely, so an id from anywhere else will be used as given. Resend it on every follow-up call for the same prospect (e.g. a `force: true` after `duplicates_found`); inputs are not remembered between calls.

recordId.description: Enrich this existing Salesforce Lead or Contact instead of creating a new record. Send it after a previous call returned `status: "record_choice_required"` and a human picked one of the `records`. Sending it skips the duplicate search entirely, so a record id from anywhere else will be updated as given.

updateExisting.description: Allow this export to update a Salesforce record that already matches this person, instead of only ever inserting. Mirrors the LeadIQ web app's "Update existing and create new" vs "Only export new" choice. Left false the export is insert-only, which is how this endpoint has always behaved. When true and exactly one record matches it is enriched; when several match you get `record_choice_required`.

matches.description: Never empty — a ref only appears here when at least one candidate matched.

entityType.description: Salesforce object of the candidate, e.g. `Lead`.

personId.description: The record's mapped `IQ_Person_Id__c` (a LeadIQ id), not the Salesforce id.

strict.description: Default false. When false, LeadIQ first enriches any missing match fields (e.g. email) before checking Salesforce, improving recall. When true, only the fields you supply are used, with no enrichment. Spends no credits in either mode.

ref.description: Caller-assigned correlation id, echoed back on the matching duplicate entry.

domain.description: The email domain of the members of this team.

409.description: A list with this name already exists

allOf.description: Filter to lists where the caller has this role. Omitted = both owner and collaborator.

parameters.description: Filter to lists where the caller has this role. Omitted = both owner and collaborator.
parameters.name: role

200.description: Lists accessible to the caller (as owner or collaborator).

404.description: Not found or not accessible to caller
Not found or not accessible to caller

post.summary: Save a prospect to a list (create, or partial-update on match)
post.description:
Saves a prospect to the given list. If the body matches a prospect the caller already owns — by `personId`, then `workEmail`, then exact `firstName`+`lastName`+`company` — that prospect is **partially updated** and attached to the list, and the response is `200`. Otherwise a new prospect is created and attached, and the response is `201`.

**Partial-update semantics on match:** only fields present in the body are written; absent fields keep their stored values (a previously verified email, location, or company data is never cleared by a save that omits it). Sent fields are stored verbatim — `title` is not normalized, and `seniority`/`function` are not re-derived from it. There is currently no way to clear a field through this endpoint.

**Retries:** re-sending the same body is safe on match (it updates the same prospect). A retry after a network error can still double-create when the first attempt succeeded but carried no `personId`/`workEmail` and a differing name/company; clients that retry should prefer sending a `personId`.

200.description: Existing prospect partially updated and attached to the list

404.description: List not found or not accessible to caller

504.description: Save timed out with the outcome unconfirmed — the prospect may exist; check before retrying

post.summary: Save multiple prospects to a list (batch)
post.description:
Saves up to 100 prospects in one call and attaches them all to the given list. Each item follows the same rule as the single-save endpoint: an item matching a prospect the caller already owns (by `personId`, `workEmail`, or exact name+company) partially updates that prospect — absent fields keep their stored values — while non-matching items create new prospects. Two items for the same person within one batch are not cross-checked; send one item per person.

**Partial-success semantics:** the response always returns 200 if the request is well-formed and the caller owns the list. The body contains `succeeded[]` and `failed[]`. `failed[i].index` refers to the position of the failing item in the request body array. Successes appear in `succeeded[]` in input order; failures are sorted by `index`.

**Retries** are safe for items that match existing prospects (they update in place); items without a `personId`/`workEmail` match can still double-create.

200.description: Per-item result; check failed[] for partial failures

404.description: List not found or not accessible to caller

post.summary: Attach an existing prospect to a list
post.description: Attaches an existing prospect to the given list. **Idempotent** — calling twice with the same `(listId, prospectId)` pair both return 200 and the resulting `listIds` array contains the list id once, not twice. The caller must be able to access the destination list (owner or collaborator). The prospect must either already be a member of one of the caller's accessible lists, or have been created standalone by the same caller via `POST /v1/prospects`. The 200 body is the post-update prospect with the new `listIds`.

404.description: List or prospect not found or not accessible to caller

200.description: Company lists owned by the caller.

409.description: A company list with this name already exists (`conflict`), or the caller already has 500 company lists (`company_list_limit_reached`)

404.description: Not found or not accessible to caller

patch.summary: Rename a company list or change its description
patch.description: Partial update: send only the fields to change. `name` must stay unique among the caller's lists (case-insensitive), the same rule as on create. `description` set to `null` or to an empty string clears it; leaving it out keeps the current value.

400.description: Invalid body (empty, unknown fields, or blank name)

404.description: Not found or not accessible to caller

409.description: Another company list of the caller already has this name (`conflict`)

delete.description: Permanently deletes the list and removes every company from it. This cannot be undone. The companies themselves are not affected: they stay captured for the organization and in any other lists. A list that contains prospects is refused with 409, so this can never destroy a prospect list.

200.description: List deleted; `deletedCompanies` counts the removed entries

404.description: Not found or not accessible to caller

409.description: The list contains prospects (`list_has_prospects`). Company-list calls never delete a list that holds people; remove them in the app first.

200.description: Companies in the list, newest first

403.description: No organization could be resolved for the caller (`org_required`). Companies in lists are stored per organization.

404.description: Not found or not accessible to caller

post.summary: Save a company to a list (create, or partial-update on match)
post.description:
Saves a company into the given list. If it matches an entry already in the list — by `companyId`, then `domain`, then `linkedinUrl`, then exact `name` — that entry is **partially updated** (only sent fields are written; absent fields keep their stored values) and the response is `200`. Otherwise a new entry is created and the response is `201`. Re-saving the same company is therefore safe and never duplicates.

Companies can come from a company search (send the result `id` as `companyId` — the strongest match key) or be added manually by `name`, `domain`, and/or `linkedinUrl`. The save stores what you send verbatim (`domain` lowercased): it never resolves, enriches, or spends credits.

403.description: No organization could be resolved for the caller (`org_required`). Companies in lists are stored per organization.

404.description: List not found or not accessible to caller

post.summary: Save multiple companies to a list (batch)
post.description:
Saves up to 100 companies in one call. Each item follows the same rule as the single-save endpoint: a match on an existing entry (by `companyId` → `domain` → `linkedinUrl` → exact `name`) partially updates it, everything else creates a new entry. Items are processed in order and each item sees the writes of earlier items, so two items for the same company within one batch converge onto a single entry.

**Partial-success semantics:** a well-formed request against an accessible list always returns 200. `succeeded[]` preserves input order and interleaves created and updated entries (`created`/`updated` count them); `failed[i].index` refers to the request array position.

200.description: Per-item result; check failed[] for partial failures

403.description: No organization could be resolved for the caller (`org_required`). Companies in lists are stored per organization.

404.description: List not found or not accessible to caller

delete.summary: Remove a company from a list
delete.description: Removes one entry from the list. `companyEntryId` is the entry `id` returned when listing the companies in a list (not the DataIQ `companyId`). Returns the removed entry, which can be re-added later.

200.description: Entry removed; body is the removed entry

403.description: No organization could be resolved for the caller (`org_required`). Companies in lists are stored per organization.

404.description: List or entry not found, or not accessible to caller

get.description: Find prospects across all of the caller's leads, regardless of list membership. Pass **either** `email` alone, **or** `firstName` + `lastName` together, **or** no criteria to list every prospect the caller owns. Half-name searches and combined email+name are rejected with 400.

post.summary: Save a prospect without a list (create, or partial-update on match)
post.description:
Saves a prospect with no list membership. Use `POST /v1/lists/{listId}/prospects` instead to save-and-attach in a single call.

Follows the same save semantics as that endpoint: a body matching a prospect the caller already owns (by `personId`, then `workEmail`, then exact `firstName`+`lastName`+`company`) **partially updates** it — absent fields keep their stored values — and returns `200`; otherwise a new prospect is created and returned with `201`.

504.description: Save timed out with the outcome unconfirmed — the prospect may exist; check before retrying

get.description: Verify any email without creating or modifying a lead. Useful as a pre-flight check before creating a prospect. The verdict is computed by EVS (Email Verification Service) and folded into our four-value status enum.

404.description: Not found or not visible to caller

post.summary: Verify the email on an existing prospect
post.description: Verifies the email currently stored on the lead and persists the new status. The lead's `workEmail` field is **never** modified — this is a verify-what's-there operation, not a discover-and-replace one. Returns 409 with `code: "no_email_to_verify"` if the lead has no email (a state precondition, not a body-validation failure).

404.description: Not found or not visible to caller

409.description: Lead has no email to verify (state precondition)

post.summary: Export a prospect into the caller's Salesforce
post.description:
Creates (or enriches) a Lead or Contact in the Salesforce org connected to the calling user, using the same export pipeline as the LeadIQ web app. Acts as the caller's connected Salesforce user, so their Salesforce permissions, validation rules and duplicate rules all still apply.

**Writes to an external system of record and cannot be undone by this API.** There is no delete path, and this endpoint is **not idempotent** — retrying may create a second record.

Whether the prospect is saved as a Lead or a Contact is decided by the member's `Save to` setting and the org's governance; it is deliberately not selectable here.

May consume Universal Credits when the prospect carries a DataIQ company id that the org has not already unlocked — the export unlocks company data to populate the Salesforce Account.

`200` reports a terminal outcome, **including `duplicates_found`, where nothing was written.** `202` means the export was handed off but its outcome is unknown; do not retry on a `202`.

200.description: Terminal outcome (created, updated, or duplicates found)

202.description: Submitted; terminal outcome unknown. Do not retry.

403.description: `salesforce_export_disabled` — a LeadIQ admin has disabled Salesforce export for this org; or `salesforce_export_not_enabled` — the feature is still rolling out and is not enabled for the caller's team yet

404.description: Not found or not visible to caller

502.description: Temporary upstream error — safe to retry

post.summary: Check people against the caller's connected Salesforce for duplicates
post.description: Read-only: for each submitted person, reports whether they already exist as a Lead or Contact in the caller's connected Salesforce. **Duplicates-only** — a person not present in the response is net-new; the response never echoes non-duplicates. **Spends no credits.** The optional batch `strict` flag controls matching: `false` (default) first enriches any missing match fields before checking Salesforce, for better recall; `true` matches only on the fields supplied, with no enrichment. Free either way. Side-effect-free and safe to retry.

200.description: Duplicates found among the submitted people (may be empty)

409.description: State precondition: `salesforce_not_connected` — this LeadIQ user has no connected Salesforce account; or `member_not_in_team` — this LeadIQ user is not in a team, so Salesforce field mappings cannot be resolved

502.description: Transient upstream/Salesforce-check failure — safe to retry

get.description: Returns the account behind the presented credentials: the user identity this API scopes ownership by, plus the team name and email domain. Useful for verifying which account an API key or token belongs to.
